finding1.cause: PostTurnReflector reflects the complete session but tags journal/candidate with input turn and calculates pollution only for that input turn.
finding1.observed: Old MCP failure is quarantined on its own turn, then the same old evidence is queued as pending and relabeled with a new successful clean turn and task goal.
finding1.securityLimit: This weakens quarantine provenance. It does not prove automatic promotion or bypass of later security/evaluation/sandbox gates; explicit learn promotion remains required.
finding1.minimalFix: Project the target turn's event stream in Harness before reflection; pass the same projected events to Reflector and pollution detector. Keep Reflector's general session stream API unchanged.

finding2.cause: Journal append reads the full journal then calls writeFile without a mutex. Concurrent sessions read identical snapshots and overwrite each other's receipts.
finding2.observed: Ten repetitions of 20 concurrent sessions: 200 outputs announced and 200 candidate records, but 10 surviving journal rows.
finding2.minimalFix: Use the existing @ar/store-integrity withLock keyed by normalized journal path and appendDurable for each JSONL record. Preserve catch-and-report error compatibility; no whole-journal rewrite. No cross-process locking claim.

legacyAttribution: An event's explicit outer turnId is authoritative; contradictory current boundary cannot retag it.

For untagged legacy events, use an unambiguous current turn.started boundary through that turn's terminal boundary. Boundary payload.turnId can identify legacy turn boundaries when outer turnId is missing.
Untagged current-turn tool requests/failures/completions must remain correlated and pollution quarantine must remain effective.
Old-turn untagged MCP requests must not contaminate a current clean turn.

Do not claim orphan events outside a known turn span as belonging to the requested current turn. For fully untagged/boundary-free history, attribution cannot be recovered reliably; prefer observable exclusion rather than guessing or silently dequarantining.
acceptance: The original built production reproducer demonstrates baseline failure. A candidate-mode verification of the exact same scenario gives old turn one quarantined candidate and new clean turn zero outputs/candidates; old evidence is never relabeled.
Current explicit failure still creates the original expected candidate/structured evidence, and current MCP pollution still creates quarantined candidates.

Current untagged failures inside identifiable boundaries still reflect; old untagged failure/MCP rows do not replay or leak pollution into later turn; unknown/orphan rows are not assigned to the target turn.
Two turns reusing a toolCallId cannot correlate an old request or later recovery across the target boundary.
Current permission and sandbox denials stay non-generalizable; injection/secret memory-write rejections produce the original audit events and no queued candidate.
All 20 current independent sessions retain 20 unique parseable journal records, with 20 candidates and unchanged announced output counts, across repeated concurrent runs.
Different PostTurnReflector instances pointing at the same journal in one process do not lose or interleave records.
Append preserves pre-existing schema-1 journal lines byte-for-byte; listJournal continues to read them and reports corrupt lines without rewriting history.

Journal write failure remains contained and reported. The baseline announces one output even when the journal write fails; preserve this compatibility or explicitly document any truthful count semantic change.
A failed journal append does not poison the mutex chain: a subsequent valid append succeeds.

Event list errors remain contained and reported; candidate-store add errors remain contained and candidates stays zero; write-gate denial event-store append failures still propagate as audit failures.
Existing Harness reflection and Memory reflection tests, relevant security/integration tests, typecheck, and full suite pass on the final frozen code revision.
excluded: No model or paid API calls
No changes to default strategy, Runtime architecture, security policy, or learning promotion gate
No claim that previously persisted incorrect candidates are repaired by this forward-path fix
No synthetic or patched production implementation was used in the reproducer
